proofs.text: For privacy, in the SUSDP protocol, each individual user ensures $( ,δ)$-DP, and the detection and recovery post processes the results from users. By parallel composition (Lemma~ [ref] ) and post processing (Lemma~ [ref] ), the SUSDP protocol satisfies $( ,δ)$-DP. For utility, let $q$ denote the ID of the corrupted user, and $ I = \ 1,2, ,n\ \ q\ $ denote the set of IDs of honest users. If the corrupted user sends excessive noisy messages and is detected, then $ Q (D) = Σ_ i I Q _i$, and the error is bounded by \| Q (D) - Q(D)\|_ _p & = \|Σ_ i I Q _i - Q(D)\|_ _p \\ & ≤ Σ_ i I \| Q _i - Q(\ x_i\ )\|_ _p + \|0 - Q(\ x_q\ )\|_ _p \\ & ≤ (n-1) · Error _ _p ( P _Q, , δ, β/n) + γ_ _p (Q,1), with probability at least $1-β$ using the union bound. If the corrupted user manipulates its data and is not detected, there must exist $c Range (Q, 1)$ such that $\| Q _q - c\|_ _p ≤ Error _ _p ( P _Q, , δ, β/n)$. By the triangle inequality, \| Q _q - Q(\ x_q\ )\|_ _p ≤ \| Q _q - c\|_ _p + \|c-Q(\ x_q\ )\|_ _p ≤ Error _ _p ( P _Q, , δ, β/n) + γ_ _p (Q,1). As $ Q (D) = Σ_ i Q _i$ where $i \ 1, 2, , n\ $, the error is bounded by \| Q (D) - Q(D)\|_ _p = \|Σ_ i=1 ^n Q _i - Q(D)\|_ _p ≤ n · Error _ _p ( P _Q, , δ, β/n) + γ_ _p (Q,1). \\ Comparing these two bounds, it is clear that the worst-case error occurs when the attacker's malicious behavior is just not detected and their output is included in the final aggregation. In all, the total error is bounded by $n · Error _ _p ( P _Q, , δ, β/n) + γ_ _p (Q,1)$ with probability at least $1-β$. For communication cost, by the complexity of protocol $ P _Q$, each honest user sends $ Msg ( P _Q, ,δ,1)$ messages in expectation, where each message encodes two components: ; The user data cost is $ Bit ( P _Q, , δ,U,n)$ bits; ; A unique shuffler identifier requires $log n$ bits. Note that, regardless of whether the corrupted user is present, honest users always send this amount of messages in expectation, and each message follows the same format. This declaration applies to all protocols proposed in this paper that build upon the shuffle-DP model and will not be reiterated in the following sections.

By basic composition (Lemma~ [ref] ) and post processing (Lemma~ [ref] ), the whole BSDP protocol with three levels satisfies $( , δ)$-DP. For utility, let $q$ denote the ID of the corrupted user, and $b$ denotes the ID of the block with the corrupted user. The overall error of the BSDP protocol consists of two parts: i) input bias, the result difference between the true input and the corrupted input, and ii) message noise, resulting from noisy messages including both legitimate randomness from the protocol and any excessive noise injected by corrupted users. By the union bound, with probability at least $1 - β$, the message noise within each level does not exceed its respective $θ^ (r) $ threshold; any group whose deviation surpasses $θ^ (r) $ is flagged as corrupted. After recovery, the error for $ Q _b^ (2) $ is bounded by $(√ n -1)· θ^ (1) + γ_ _p (Q,1)$, and the error for $ Q ^ (3) $ is bounded by $(√ n -1)· θ^ (1) + (√ n -1) · θ^ (2) + γ_ _p (Q,1)$. If the corrupted user is detected at the block-level, from the non-detection result, the total error of recovered $ Q _b^ (2) $ is bounded by $√ n · θ^ (1) + γ_ _p (Q,1)$. The error for $ Q ^ (3) $ is then bounded by $ √ n · θ^ (1) + (√ n -1) · θ^ (2) + γ_ _p (Q,1)$. If the corrupted user is detected at the output-level, then the error for $ Q ^ (3) $ is bounded by $2√ n · θ^ (1) + √ n ·θ^ (2) + γ_ _p (Q,1)$. Similar to the proof of Theorem~ [ref] , the OHSDP protocol also satisfies $( , δ)$-DP. For utility, with probability at least $1 - β$, the message noise at level $r$ is bounded by $θ^ (r) $, for all $r \ 1, 2, , log(n/λ) + 1\ $. The main difference between OHSDP and HSDP protocols is that OHSDP aggregates level $1$ users into groups of size $λ$, which are then handled identically to higher-level groups. Unlike the proof of Theorem~ [ref] , in the OHSDP protocol, if the corrupted user is not detected at the bottom level, the error upper bound for the bottom-level group containing the corrupted user is B_1 = θ^ (1) + γ_ _p (Q, λ). If the corrupted user is detected, then the error for the same group after recovery becomes R^1_1 = γ_ _p (Q, λ). Nevertheless, this difference does not affect the conclusion that, with probability at least $1 - β$, the worst-case error in the OHSDP protocol occurs when the corrupted user evades all levels of detection. Therefore, substituting $λ = log n · log (1/δ)$, the error of the OHSDP protocol is bounded by B_ log (n/λ) + 1 = 4· θ^ (1) + + 4·θ^ (log (n/λ)) + θ^ (log (n/λ) + 1) + γ_ _p (Q,λ). with probability at least $1- β$. For privacy, an increase in the number of corrupted users does not affect the privacy guarantees of the OHSDP protocol with privacy budgets scaled by $(c - k )/ c $. Therefore, the protocol continues to satisfy $( , δ)$-DP. For utility, with probability at least $1- β$, the message noise for level $r$ falls within $θ^ (r) $ for $r \ 1, 2, , log (n/λ) + 1\ $. The upper bounds $B_1$ and $R^1_1$ for the level $1$ groups in the proof of Theorem~ [ref] still hold in the presence of multiple corrupted users. If all corrupted users evade detection, the worst-case error occurs when the $k$ corrupted users are distributed across distinct groups at the same level. In this scenario, all $k$ corrupted users remain in separate groups until the final $ log k $ levels. Moreover, since each group contains only one corrupted user, B_r = 4· θ^ (1) + 4·θ^ (2) + +4 · θ^ (r-1) + θ^ (r) + γ_ _p (Q,λ) holds for level $r \ 2, 3, …, log(n/λ) + 1 - log k \ $. As a result, at level $l = log(n/λ) + 1 - log k $, there are $k$ groups each with an error upper bound of $B_l$, while the remaining groups have errors bounded by $θ^ (l) $. Since each merge of two groups from level $r$ to level $r +1$ adds up the error of at most $2θ^ (r) + θ^ (r+1) $, with probability at least $1 -β$, the final error bound satisfies B_ log(n/λ) + 1 &≤ k · B_l + 3k· θ^ (l) + Σ_ i = l+1 ^ log(n/λ) 2^ l-i k·θ^ (i) + θ^ (log(n/λ) + 1) \\ &≤ 4k · Σ_ i = 1 ^ log (n/λ) θ^ (i) + θ^ (log(n/λ) + 1) + k· γ_ _p (Q,λ) where each \(θ^ (r) \) denotes \( Error _ _p ( P _Q, ^ (r) , δ^ (r) , β^ (r) )\), with privacy parameters allocated identically to those in the single-attacker setting (see the proof of Theorem~ [ref] ). Additionally, we can show that the worst-case error bound, with probability at least $1 - β$, arises when all detection fails. For any group at level $r > 1$, if detection and recovery occur, the post-recovery error bound is equal to the sum of the error bounds of its subgroups at level $r - 1$. In contrast, if detection fails, the error may increase by at most $2θ^ (r) + θ^ (r+1) $ beyond this base. At the bottom level , we have $B_1 ≥ R^1_1$, ensuring that the worst-case scenario remains valid at the lowest level.
